member.name: T:MelloSilveiraTools.Database.RelationalDatabase.Sql.Provider.ISqlProvider
member.summary: Provides SQL statements tailored to a specific database dialect for an entity type provided per call.

remarks.para: The SQL strings returned by this interface contain textual placeholders prefixed with # that the caller (typically ) substitutes via before execution. Implementations must keep these placeholder names stable. The placeholders currently emitted are:

item.description: #WHERE — replaced with the full WHERE ... clause built from a FilterBase, or with null/empty when no filter applies.
#ORDERBY — replaced with the ORDER BY ... clause derived from the requested SortOrder.
#LIMIT — replaced with LIMIT n for paginated queries (removed otherwise).
#OFFSET — replaced with OFFSET n for paginated queries (removed otherwise).
#JOIN — replaced with LEFT/INNER JOIN clauses derived from [ForeignKeyColumn] attributes on the entity (only present in SELECT templates).

remarks.para: Internal placeholders such as #TABLE_NAME, #TABLE_ALIAS, #COLUMNS, #VALUES, #PARAMETER_NAMES, #PRIMARY_KEY, #VALUES_TO_UPDATE, #UNIQUE_COLUMNS and #UNIQUE_UPDATES are resolved by the provider itself before the SQL is returned, and callers should not see them in the produced strings.

member.summary: Builds a SELECT … LIMIT 1 statement that filters by the entity's single [UniqueColumn]-annotated column.
member.remarks: The SQL parameter name is the **fixed literal** @UniqueColumnValue regardless of the underlying property name, so callers don't need to know the entity's metadata. Includes the same JOINs as (foreign-key projections), so the WHERE clause is qualified by the main table's alias to remove ambiguity when the joined tables also have a column with the same name.
member.exception: Thrown when has zero or more than one [UniqueColumn]-annotated property.

remarks.para: Generated SQL strings are memoized in a process-wide static keyed by (Type, Operation, BatchSize). Entries are never evicted: the cache lives for the entire application lifetime. Memory growth is therefore bounded by the number of entity types multiplied by the number of supported operations (and, for bulk inserts, by the number of distinct batch sizes used).

This provider is NOT multi-tenant safe when different tenants map the same CLR type to different schemas or table names: the cached SQL is keyed only by , not by tenant context. Use a separate provider instance (or distinct entity types per tenant) when schema isolation is required.

member.summary: Provides a generic, filter-driven abstraction over persistent storage for entity types.
member.remarks:
All asynchronous members accept a and will throw when cancellation is signalled.
Transient database failures (connection drops, broken protocol, network blips, command timeouts caused by transient conditions) are absorbed and retried resilience pipeline. Once the pipeline budget is exhausted the underlying exceptions are re-thrown to the caller. Non-transient failures — for example unique-constraint violations, permission errors, or definitive command timeouts — are not retried and are propagated as .
